name: Couto Misto (until 1868)
description: A square field divided vertically white at the hoist and blue at the fly.
history: The Couto Misto was a tiny self-governing territory of three villages on the border of Galicia and Portugal that answered to neither crown from the Middle Ages. It was partitioned by the Treaty of Lisbon of 29 September 1864 and absorbed by Spain in 1868. Its square white-and-blue flag is known from the memoirs of Delfim Modesto Brandão, its last judge, published in 1907.
